messages:
Sara K: Heads up — Prospect Bluebridge asked for a Dedicated commit: 1.5k GPU-hours/week (A100-equivalent) with burst allowance to 2.5k GPU-hours/week during a Q3 marketing push. Need recommended commit sizing + buffer policy + quick pricing delta. @Olivia P @Mike L
Olivia P: 👍 Sales flagged that the campaign is critical for them, they want low risk of throttling. They also asked if burst can be automatic vs approval.
Mike L: Quick clarification: is that 1.5k/week steady state or their average?
Sara K: They said "commit 1.5k/week" as baseline and expect spikes up to 2.5k for 2–3 weeks in the quarter.
Mike L: Ok math (week = 168h). Sustained GPUs = 1500 / 168 ≈ 8.93 -> ~9 GPUs. Burst 2500 / 168 ≈ 14.88 -> ~15 GPUs.
Mike L: Paste calc: ```
# sustained_gpus = gpu_hours / hours_per_week
sustained = 1500 / 168  # ~8.93
burst = 2500 / 168      # ~14.88
```
Raj S: For dedicated commits we usually ask for 1) baseline commit ~steady GPUs 2) buffer/headroom (10–30%) 3) burst policy with limits and time windows. For this ask I'd propose: baseline commit = 10 GPUs (rounded up), buffer = 25% of commit, burst cap = 1.5x commit by default for up to 168 hours/month, further burst allowed with dynamic pricing.
Ben T: From sales: customers want predictable costs. If we require a 25% headroom on top of 10 GPUs => effective commit = 12.5 GPUs -> round to 13 GPUs (~2184 GPU-hours/week). That's pretty different from their request. Need a compromise.
Olivia P: They pushed back on big uplifts. Can we do a smaller commit but allow scheduled burst windows tied to campaign dates?
Mike L: We can do scheduled burst windows (can reserve capacity) — that reduces our risk. Alternative: commit 10 GPUs, buffer pool of 3 GPUs reserved in same region for quick failover, and burst window up to 15 GPUs for a defined 2-week campaign window.
autoscale-bot: capacity-forecast: region us-west-2 has a scheduled node maintenance on 2026-07-10..2026-07-12; expected regional GPU capacity -12% during that window.
Raj S: Important: if Bluebridge insists on US-West residency during their campaign, the maintenance window could impact available burst capacity. Recommend cross-region failover option to us-east or a guaranteed reserved burst pool as part of the contract.
Ben T: Pricing sketch: if baseline commit = 10 GPUs (1500h/w = ~12000h/month? wait units), simpler to quote in GPU-hours: baseline 1500h/week, burst allowance up to 2500h/week for two 1-week windows per quarter. Overage beyond burst billed at 1.5x; scheduled burst included at no extra markup up to 1.2x of commit; instantaneous burst beyond that requires approval.
Olivia P: TL;DR for customer: keep their cost predictable and give them 2 scheduled campaign bursts.
Mike L: Draft clause suggestion: "Burst policy: scheduled campaign windows up to 2 weeks/quarter where burst permitted up to 2.5k GPU-hours/week. On-demand burst allowed up to 1.5x commit for up to 72h/month. Overage beyond burst billed at 1.5x standard rate. We reserve the right to route to alternative region if capacity constrained; customer will be notified 48h in advance unless emergency."
Sara K: Action items: I'll propose two SKU options: 1) Conservative: Commit 13 GPUs (25% buffer) + 2 scheduled burst windows (no markup up to 2.5k/week) 2) Lean: Commit 10 GPUs + reserved 3-GPU burst pool (additional monthly fee) + on-demand burst (approval, billed at 1.5x). I'll send to legal + sales.
Raj S: Operational note: if we choose reserved burst pool, we need to guarantee placement in same AZ or accept cross-AZ latency. Also check KMS/data residency constraints if routing cross-region.
Ben T: I'll prep the pricing delta numbers and customer-facing sheet.
Olivia P: I can confirm campaign dates with Bluebridge and push for scheduled windows.
Mike L: +1. If anyone wants to simulate cost/availability for the two SKUs, ping me and I'll run quick cluster placement sims.
Sara K: Thanks team — I'll follow up with a proposal draft by EOD tomorrow. :calendar:
